sections.heading: C2 — Learner permit and Class C licensing
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Learner permit and Class C licensing

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A02
At license renewal, the applicant is asked whether the license should carry an organ-donor designation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A02
Saying yes to organ-donor designation at the Photo License Center puts that designation on the driver license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
An applicant younger than 18 may obtain organ-donor designation only with written consent from a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
The adult may give a minor's organ-donor consent through the appropriate box on DL-180TD. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
The organ-donor designation can also be added to the driver record through PennDOT's website, which offers a card to print and carry with the license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
A voluntary organ-donation awareness contribution is marked on the license form and included with the license-fee payment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A02
Veteran designation requires qualifying service, including reserve or National Guard service, with discharge or release under conditions other than dishonorable. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A03
A voluntary Veterans' Trust Fund contribution is additional to the licensing fee and should be identified by the proper form box. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A03
PennDOT collects the applicant's Social Security number, height and eye color as identifying information to reduce license fraud. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A03
The Social Security number is excluded from the public driver record. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A03
A Social Security number is not displayed on the learner permit or driver license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A03
Poor sight in one eye does not necessarily prevent licensing, though corrective lenses, daytime-only driving or side mirrors may be required. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A03
Failure to meet vision standards results in the examiner providing the DL-102 eye-examination report form. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A03
An optometrist, ophthalmologist or family physician should examine vision and complete DL-102 before the applicant returns to continue testing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A03
A valid foreign license authorizes Pennsylvania driving for up to one year after entry into the United States or until that license expires, whichever is earlier. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A03
For a foreign-license holder, an international driving permit is recommended but is not required. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A03
Reciprocity allows valid non-commercial licenses from France, Germany, Korea or Taiwan to transfer without knowledge or road testing, while a vision test remains required. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A03
Transfers from Puerto Rico, France or Germany cannot be completed within the same day. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A03
Pennsylvania residents aged at least 16 who wish to operate a motor vehicle need a Pennsylvania driver license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A03
A new Pennsylvania resident holding a valid license from another state or Canada must obtain a Pennsylvania license within 60 days of moving and surrender the former license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A03
Armed Forces personnel with a Pennsylvania legal address, including reserve members stationed there, need a driver license to operate a non-military vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A03
A junior learner permit lasts one year from the issue date shown on the initial permit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A03
A junior learner's licensed supervisor must occupy the front seat and be at least 21, or be a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A03
A junior learner cannot carry passengers exceeding the available seat belts. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R25 | anchor: A03
A junior license normally prohibits driving from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18, with additional authorized activity exceptions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R26 | anchor: A03
A junior driver may drive during the restricted nighttime hours for public or charitable service, volunteer firefighting or employment, but must carry a notarized schedule affidavit or authorization certificate from the employer, supervisor or fire chief. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R27 | anchor: A03
A junior license holder must keep the passenger count within the number of available seat belts. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R28 | anchor: A04
Without an accompanying parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18, a junior driver initially may carry only one non-immediate-family passenger younger than 18. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R29 | anchor: A04
After six months on a junior license, the limit without an accompanying parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18 rises to three non-immediate-family passengers younger than 18, except for a driver ever responsible in whole or part for a crash or convicted of a driving violation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R30 | anchor: A04
A junior driver receives a mandatory 90-day suspension for reaching six points or being convicted of exceeding the posted limit by at least 26 mph. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R31 | anchor: A04
After holding a junior license for one year, a driver may seek a regular license only with an approved driver-training course, a year free of responsible crashes and Vehicle Code convictions, and consent from a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R32 | anchor: A04
An eligible junior driver applies for early conversion to a regular non-commercial license with DL-59. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R33 | anchor: A04
A junior license becomes a regular license automatically when the holder reaches 18. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R34 | anchor: A04
The license class required in Pennsylvania depends on the type of vehicle operated. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R35 | anchor: A04
This handbook covers non-commercial Class C licensing for ordinary passenger vehicles, pickup trucks and vans. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R36 | anchor: A04
Class C requires a driver aged at least 16 who has demonstrated the qualifications for vehicles outside Classes A, B and M. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]
